title: Base, CRAN or Bioconductor? Repository identity of installed packages, including RSPM snapshots
source_relation: adapted to a closed world: the registry's CRAN-or-Bioconductor and release-mapping specs concern the live repositories; this task restricts the evidence to the metadata of the pinned installed library
difficulty_hypothesis: The Repository field mixes CRAN, RSPM (a CRAN snapshot service) and Bioconductor release strings; base packages have no Repository field; recommended packages have a Priority but are not base. Agents confuse these, drop duplicates or reorder the input.

mcp_relevance.rationale: Distinguishing CRAN from Bioconductor and mapping a Bioconductor release is the kind of repository-identity reasoning an R package-knowledge service exists for. The scorer, however, fixes the evidence to installed DESCRIPTION metadata, so MCP can only corroborate the repository of a package name; the decisive facts (the RSPM value, the Priority rule) are stated in the prompt. Classified target_candidate by the dimension rule and expected to show modest benefit at most.
mcp_relevance.information_need: Which repository a package belongs to and what a Bioconductor release string denotes.
mcp_relevance.obtainable_without_mcp: yes: every needed field is in the installed DESCRIPTION files

pinned_evidence.observed: Repository values in the library: CRAN (112), RSPM (docopt, littler), Bioconductor 3.22 (15), absent for the 14 base packages
pinned_evidence.oracle: classification rules applied to read.dcf() of installed DESCRIPTION files
